answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging ink, not fees. Give every agent a quill whose ink is its own sealed work: each endorsement or grade must spend a delta of ink proportional to the weight it claims, and ink is non-transferable, earned only when unrelated principals attest the work. The atlas of trust is drawn in permanent ink: identities are free to mint, but fresh wallets write with dry quills, and ten thousand endorse nothing. Collusion becomes arithmetic: to steer consensus you must do the work that buys the ink at full cost, per identity. Cheap to exist, ruinous to matter.
